A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ASUKA despite changes to the title and presentation. Their text, equations, figures and tables support comparison. V1's supplementary material was checked against corresponding material retained, moved or omitted in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original MISATO experiments, component ablations, qualitative analyses, and supplementary Places2 and user-study results.

after.justification: V2 reports original MISATO and Places2 comparisons, component ablations, qualitative examples and user-preference results in Tables 1–2 and the accompanying figures.

M1.justification: Both versions retain MAE guidance for frozen SD, linear and self-attention alignment, and a conditioned decoder trained with color and latent augmentation. V2's grouped mask probabilities and expanded training explanations do not establish a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Training remains on Places2, and evaluation retains Places2 plus MISATO's indoor, landscape, building and background domains. Places2 and object removal already appear in v1. V2's additional qualitative images remain within these tasks; their resolution is an experimental-setting addition.

E2.justification: V2 adds SD-Repaint to both benchmark comparisons, Figure 8 and the user study. The other comparators remain. The decoder labels 'Asy. VAE' and '+ cond.' refer to the same existing comparator.

E3.justification: V2 removes PSNR and SSIM from the evaluation metrics and changes the reported user-study criteria from consistency/quality to context stability/color consistency. It also adds explicitly 1024×1024 qualitative evaluations. Benchmark sample counts and the study's 40 images and 100 questionnaires remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether the study was rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a qualitative latent-augmentation ablation in Figure 7a. It removes v1's supplementary Section 7.3 and Figure 10 analysis of disagreement between PSNR/SSIM and perceived quality. The principal component ablations and self-attention failure case remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and average preference percentages without repeated-seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The user-study sample reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: All retained benchmark LPIPS/FID/IDS values match exactly, as do retained ablation scores. V2 adds SD-Repaint results, including FID 27.861 on MISATO and 12.466 on Places2, and removes PSNR/SSIM entries. ASUKA's user-study percentages change from 39.38/40.00 to 39.43/40.05, but changed criteria and comparator options prevent interpreting this as a same-setting gain. Additional qualitative results are also reported.

T1.justification: The dimension-alignment mathematics and one-step denoising relation in Equation 1 retain their substance. Changes to estimate symbols are notation cleanup. Neither version supplies a theoretical development or proofs that are added or removed.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that MAE guidance reduces unwanted generation while preserving frozen SD's capacity, and decoder harmonization improves masked/unmasked consistency. 'Context-stability' and 'visual-consistency' make these existing claims more explicit without introducing a different core contribution.

C2.justification: V2 explains how conflicting MAE predictions and diffusion targets can cause the alignment module to ignore its prior. It also distinguishes VAE reconstruction loss from the generated-versus-real latent distribution gap when motivating augmentation. The PSNR/SSIM interpretation is removed, while the self-attention limitation remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds project and MISATO access links, identifies COCO segments as the object-mask source, and clarifies reconstruction targets and offline latent augmentation. Conversely, it omits v1's alignment-training budget of 23K steps and batch size 64, and makes the MAE initialization source less explicit. These are documentation changes, not demonstrated setting changes.

R1.justification: V2 adds the RePaint reference and comparison positioning. It removes references to MaskGIT, the SSIM paper and Diverse Image Inpainting with Bidirectional and Autoregressive Transformers. The broader positioning relative to GANs, diffusion, MAE and asymmetric decoders remains similar.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the introduction and method explanations around context stability and visual consistency, changes the title and author list, and integrates the supplementary Places2 evaluation and user study into the main narrative. This extends beyond terminology replacement.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document from two columns to one, replaces the opening comparison, adds object-removal examples and an alignment schematic, and combines existing figures into multipanel displays. It merges benchmark tables, groups ablations and the user study into Table 2, adds SD-Repaint displays, and removes the supplementary metric-annotated figure.

improvement.justification: V2's clearer explanations of alignment failure and decoder augmentation, new diagnostic visuals, SD-Repaint comparison and dataset-access pointers modestly improve understandability and usefulness. These gains are limited by the omission of alignment-training steps and batch size, and the loss of PSNR/SSIM results and their diagnostic analysis. The retained benchmark scores provide no evidence of improved method performance.
